primitives.verbatim_quote: Bain puts it : "In its essential character, belief is a phase of our active natureotherwise called the Will."\ The object of belief, then, reality or real existence, is something quite different from all the other predicates which a subject may possess.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that belief is not a passive reception of truth but an active volitional act—'the Will.' This implies that belief operates on a different logical plane than other predicates. Adding predicates to a concept enriches its structure, but adding 'existence' does not. This is formalized through the notion that reality is not an additive property but a stamp or marker. In GSI, this translates into a Bayesian framework where belief states are updated via Will-phase vectors rather than information gain. In GSE, it implies that existential assertions stabilize models without expanding them. The Kantian principle that 'real contains no more than possible' ensures that reality is not a source of additional information beyond what is already logically contained in the possible. Thus, the epistemic structure is preserved while the existential assertion merely fixes the model's grounding.
